analysis.title: Holding in October, hiking in December
key_insights: The Fed held the funds rate at 3.75%-4.00% as expected, and the statement kept a tightening bias. UBS expects hikes in December and March.

The statement upgraded economic activity to a "strong pace" after upward revisions to first-half growth and an expectation of 3% growth in 3Q. The labor market is resilient and inflation is still elevated.

The reference to the "accumulation of more information" explained the October pause while leaving flexibility for December. UBS reads Warsh's comments as gradual recalibration, not aggressive demand restraint.
The vote was 10-2. Governor Cook and President Hammack dissented in favor of tightening. Logan and Kashkari supported the hold, which UBS reads as comfort with waiting until December.
Warsh declined to validate a December hike, avoided forward guidance and said the December decision was not predetermined.

The press conference was more dovish than the statement. Warsh pointed to improvement in inflation compensation and inflation expectations despite firm recent inflation data, and to tighter financial and credit conditions since September.
Warsh said overall financial conditions are tighter but he was "unwilling and unable to call them tight". UBS reads this as a sign the tightening cycle is not over.
Warsh pushed back on the idea that strong AI-driven investment and growth are necessarily inflationary, citing stronger productivity and broader capital spending.

The Fed will keep eight FOMC meetings in 2027, but one next fall will cover monetary-policy strategy only, leaving seven rate-setting meetings. In 2028 Warsh expects two strategy meetings and six policy meetings. UBS sees no clear directional implication, though fewer meetings could affect the cadence of moves.
The balance-sheet task force's recommendations should reach the FOMC early in 1Q27. UBS expects any balance-sheet changes to be gradual and unlikely to affect the current policy cycle materially.
Front-end rates fell during the press conference. Cumulative tightening priced through December 2027 fell about 8bps over the meeting, and equities were comparatively muted amid earnings releases.
October inflation data is the key intermeeting release. September core PCE is expected at 0.3% m/m, so UBS sees a high bar to derail a December hike.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held as expected with a tightening bias retained. UBS expects hikes in December and March.
The expectation of 3% 3Q growth, together with upward revisions to first-half growth, led the statement to describe activity as strong.
Expected tomorrow. UBS sees the bar to derail a December hike as high.

tension_points.bull_case: The statement kept a tightening bias, activity was upgraded to a strong pace, and Cook and Hammack dissented for tightening. UBS expects hikes in December and March.
tension_points.bear_case: The press conference was dovish. Warsh refused forward guidance, said December was not predetermined, and pointed to improving inflation expectations and tighter financial conditions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS says the bar to derail a December hike is high given expected 0.3% m/m September core PCE. The October inflation data is the key intermeeting release.

theme_stances.key_argument: The statement, the voting pattern and resilient labor and inflation data support further gradual tightening.
